newsitem.title: USA: Waban's sees Q2 charge from BJ's spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Waban's sees Q2 charge from BJ's spin-off.

text.p: Waban Inc said Thursday it expects a significant second-quarter charge related to the spin-off of its BJ's Wholesale Club division, on which shareholders vote today.

"Waban's second-quarter financial statements will not be comparable to prior period reports because of significant nonrecurring expenses related to the spin-off and debt retirement," chief executive Herbert Zarkin said in a statement.
Zarkin added he expected BJ's second-quarter operating income to be 10 percent higher than last year.
A Waban spokeswoman said Thursday shareholders will vote on the proposed BJ's spin-off today. The company will declare a dividend this afternoon, she added.

Waban in October 1996 announced the spin-off, which will create two companies: BJ's Wholesale and Waban, which will rename itself HomeBase. Waban shareholders will receive one BJ's share for each Waban share, the spokeswoman said.
BJ's will have a seperate listing on the New York Stock Exchange and start trading July 29, the spokeswoman added.
Waban Thursday reported a 3.8 percent rise in BJ's same-store sales in the five weeks ended July 5, but a 6.3 percent drop in HomeBase's same-store revenues.
"HomeBase is a little more fragile (than BJ's)," the spokeswoman said, adding the company expected HomeBase to report a flat operating income in the second quarter.
Waban's stock traded at 31-3/4 Thursday morning, down 7/8.
